stage1.impression: A dim back-bar of procedurally labelled bottles with one cream-and-glass speaker standing in a dark recess at centre, and a flat brown floor taking the bottom quarter. The lit shelf backs outshine the product, the clear acrylic reads as a dark frame around a white board rather than glowing material, and the bottles' repeated banded labels and uniform shapes read as game assets. It is a layout proof, not a photograph.

blocking_9: The speaker is the brightest, clearest thing in the frame: its region's median luminance is above the shelf backs', not 23 against 105-120 as now
The clear-white acrylic reads as lit, translucent material, with light passing through its edges and the batts glowing, not as a dark frame
Bottles are varied, believable assets with real labels, glass refraction and liquid, with no repeated label pattern
Both speakers of the Fog pair are in frame, and the foreground is the bar top, not a quarter-frame of dead floor
One coherent warm colour temperature across the shelves (now cool-blue left, warm-red right)
The floor has real material detail and reflects the lit shelves and the speaker
Atmosphere: haze that shows the spot beams and separates the planes

defects.what: the speaker body is underlit (median 22.8) and darker than the shelf backs around it; the woofer reads as a black hole
the acrylic top reads as a smoky glass box with a dark blob inside; there is no edge glow or transmitted light
left shelf backs are cool blue-white (b 131 > r 116), brighter than the hero
right shelf backs are warm (r 134, b 85), so the two sides disagree in white balance
the floor is a flat, featureless brown field (lum range 19, median 21) taking about 22% of the frame
bottles repeat the same banded red and cream labels and a few silhouettes; they read as CG
the niche's back wall has speckle texture like noise or dirt, and is brighter (median 73) than the speaker in front of it
a red neon strip at the top edge is cut by the frame and pulls the eye out of the image
the right niche edge and the dark vertical post crowd the speaker; the pair's second speaker is not visible
the speaker's base sits in black with no contact shadow or bounce visible; its weight and floor contact do not read

changes.problem: The hero speaker is the darkest object in the middle of the frame and reads as a silhouette, not as glowing acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 22.8, mean 48.4; woofer area 540,460-640,590 median 15.9; shelf backs 105-120

change.setting: on each Fog speaker 2 x spot (and Fog niches)
change.from: 2 x spot 320 W, cone 30 deg; Fog niches 0.03
change.to: 2 x spot 650 W, cone 40 deg, aimed at the cabinet's mid-height from 30 deg above and either side; plus a soft area lamp at the niche's floor, behind the speaker, 10 W, so light passes up through the clear acrylic's edges

changes.expected: The cabinet reads cream-white and translucent, its edges glowing, the speaker's median luminance near 55-70.

changes.problem: The edge-lit shelves out-shine the product and pull the eye to the bottles.

evidence.measured: lum_median 120.1 left, 105.1 right (880,30-1190,180), against the speaker's 22.8

changes.expected: The shelf backs sit about a stop below the speaker, so the speaker reads first.

changes.problem: The left shelves are cool blue while the right are warm red-orange, two white balances in one room.

change.from: cool white on the left bays, warm or red-tinted on the right
change.to: one 2700 K warm white for every shelf's edge light; keep coloured light only from the speakers' own acrylic

changes.expected: Both sides of the back-bar share one warm white; the blue cast on the left is gone.

changes.problem: The frame shows one speaker and a quarter-frame of dead floor instead of the pair seen from a bar stool across the bar top.

evidence.measured: floor fills 22% of the frame, lum_range 19; the second Fog speaker is out of frame

change.to: position [3.42 + half the pair's spacing, 6.6, 1.45] centred between the two Fog niches, target z 1.1, level, 28 mm, f/4, focus on the nearer Fog speaker; place it so the honed stone bar top crosses the bottom 12-15% of the frame, out of focus, with two props (a rocks glass, a coupe) on it

changes.expected: Both Fog speakers are in frame as the subject, the bar top is the foreground, and there is depth from foreground to back-bar.

changes.problem: The floor is a uniform brown with no texture or reflection, so nothing sits on it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 21.1, lum_range 19.0, profile 12-22 with no structure

change.to: dark honed concrete with fine aggregate and pores, roughness 0.35 with a roughness map, so it carries soft reflections of the shelves and the speaker; if c4 frames the bar top in the foreground this matters less

changes.expected: Soft reflections of the speaker and the shelf glow on the floor; visible micro-texture.

changes.problem: The bottles are a small set of procedural shapes with repeated banded labels and read as a game asset.

evidence.measured: seen: the same red and cream bands repeat on more than 20 bottles; the glass shows no refraction of the lit back

change.to: 15-20 distinct modelled bottles (whisky, gin, amaro, sake) with paper labels in a few type styles, real glass (IOR 1.5, thickness), liquid at varied fills, and a few back-lit through their liquid; fewer per shelf, spaced like a curated kissa shelf

changes.expected: The shelves read as a real, curated bar; the glass refracts the lit back panel.

changes.problem: There is no atmosphere: the spot beams and planes do not separate, and the frame reads flat.

evidence.measured: lum_median 9.0, lum_p5 7.8: the lower back-bar is a flat black

changes.expected: The Fog spots show soft beams, the shadows lift slightly, and the back-bar separates from the speakers.

changes.problem: A cut-off red neon strip at the top edge and a speckled niche wall distract from the speaker.

evidence.measured: niche back median 72.9, brighter than the speaker, with visible specks; red strip at 415,0-780,40

change.setting: niche wall material and the red strip above the niche
change.to: a clean, matte warm-grey plaster with no specks; turn off the red strip above the Fog niches or crop it out with c4

changes.expected: A calm, even field behind the acrylic top, darker than the speaker, with nothing red at the frame edge.

out_of_scope.request: Make the horn inside the clear top read as a designed form rather than a dark blob
out_of_scope.why: The horn is the speaker's own part (and its shape is fixed); only light can help it, through c1

out_of_scope.request: Make the cabinet's frame and battens read less like a dark cage around a white board
out_of_scope.why: The cabinet's construction and the Fog colour are fixed; c1's transmitted light is the in-scope fix
